content.content:
version: 1
level: L3
stack: python
capture: github-issues
spec_location: docs/specs
# Django convention: tests live per-app as apps/*/tests.py, plus helpers/tests.py.
# There is no central tests/ directory.
test_location: apps
audit_state_file: .ffflow/audit.yaml

# NOTE: the python stack cartridge declares max_level: L2 on the assumption that
# specdrive is npm-only and therefore Python-incompatible. That is a packaging
# assumption, not a capability limit: specdrive is a language-agnostic CLI
# (github:bryonjacob/specdrive) that consumes JUnit XML, so it works fine against
# a Django suite. This project runs at L3 deliberately, overriding that cap.
features:
  property_based_testing: true
  mutation_testing: true
  rid_traceability: true
  four_quality_gates: true
---
CLAUDE.md
audit.yaml
config.yaml
---justfile---
set shell := ["bash", "-uc"]

# Show all available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install dependencies and setup development environment
dev-install:
    make sync
    npm install --silent  # node tooling: specdrive (L3 spec audit), Playwright

# Format code (auto-fix)
format:
    uv run ruff format .

# Lint code (auto-fix, complexity threshold=10)
lint:
    make lint

# Type check code
typecheck:
    make type-check

# Run unit tests
test:
    make test-django-fast

# Run unit tests with coverage threshold (96%)
coverage:
    DEBUG=True DATABASE_URL="file:memdb1?mode=memory&cache=shared" USE_FAST_HASHER=True uv run --with coverage coverage run -m manage test apps helpers
    uv run --with coverage coverage report --fail-under=96
    uv run --with coverage coverage html
    @echo "📊 HTML report: htmlcov/index.html"

# Run integration tests with coverage report (no threshold)
integration-test:
    npm install --silent
    npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
    cd playwright && npx playwright test

# Detailed complexity report for refactoring decisions
complexity:
    uv run --with radon radon cc apps helpers config -a -s --no-assert

# Show N largest files by lines of code
loc N="20":
    cloc apps helpers config --by-file --quiet | head -n $(({{N}} + 5))

# Install FFFlow git hooks (pre-commit framework, delegates to justfile recipes)
hooks-install:
    @if command -v pre-commit >/dev/null; then \
        pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push; \
    else \
        echo "pre-commit not found — install it (uv tool install pre-commit) then re-run."; \
        exit 1; \
    fi

# Validate spec RIDs: format, uniqueness, context-match (FFFlow L3, blocking)
spec-audit:
    npx specdrive audit

1	# templates/
2	
3	Django templates. Split into full-page templates and HTMX partials.
4	
5	## Layout
6	
7	```
8	templates/
9	  base.html              # Root layout — navbar, footer, conduit JS bootstrap
10	  accounts/              # Full-page templates for the accounts app
11	    login.html
12	    register.html
13	    settings.html
14	    profile.html         # Used by articles.views.profile_view (not accounts/)
15	    profile_404.html
16	  articles/              # Full-page templates for the articles app
17	    home.html
18	    detail.html
19	    detail_404.html
20	    editor.html
21	  partials/              # HTMX fragment templates (rendered for HX-Request)
22	    header.html
23	    footer.html
24	    feed_content.html    # The feed portion of home.html — returned for HTMX feed swaps
25	    article_list.html    # List of article preview cards
26	    article_meta.html    # Author + date + favorite button for one article
27	    favorite_button.html # Just the favorite button (swap target)
28	    follow_button.html   # Just the follow button (swap target)
29	    comment_list.html    # Entire comment thread (swap target for create/delete)
30	```
31	
32	## Conventions
33	
34	- **Full-page templates** extend `base.html` and are rendered on normal (non-HTMX) requests.
35	- **Partials** are standalone fragments with no `{% extends %}`. They are returned when `is_htmx(request)` is true, and they are also `{% include %}`-ed by the full-page templates so there is a single source of truth.
36	- **Swap granularity is the partial**: if HTMX targets `#favorite-button`, the view returns `partials/favorite_button.html` and the server sends just the button. The full-page template also `{% include %}`s the same partial, so the first paint and subsequent swaps render identically.
37	- **`templates/accounts/profile.html` lives in `accounts/` but is rendered from `articles/views.py::profile_view`**. The template location matches the URL namespace, not the code location. This is intentional (see the `refactor-pass` epic) — don't move it.
38	
39	## Selectors contract
40	
41	The RealWorld e2e suite in `realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md` pins specific CSS classes, `name` attributes, and text strings. Before renaming any of the following, grep the SELECTORS contract:
42	
43	- `<nav class="navbar">`, `<a class="navbar-brand">`, `<a class="nav-link">`
44	- `input[name="email"]`, `input[name="password"]`, `input[name="username"]`, `input[name="title"]`, `input[name="description"]`, `textarea[name="body"]`, `input[name="image"]`, `textarea[name="bio"]`
45	- Tab labels `Your Feed`, `Global Feed`, `My Articles`, `Favorited Articles`
46	- Button text `Sign in`, `Sign up`, `Publish Article`
47	
48	Breaking these is how you get a working app that fails the e2e suite.
49

1	# helpers/
2	
3	Cross-app utilities. Zero reverse dependencies — helpers depends on nothing else in the project, everything else depends on it.
4	
5	## Modules
6	
7	- **pagination.py** — `paginate(queryset, request, per_page)` + `Page` dataclass. Parses `?page=` from query string, slices the queryset, returns items + page number + page range for template rendering. Invalid input (non-int, zero, negative) defaults to page 1 — **do not use Django's built-in `Paginator`**, which raises on invalid input and breaks e2e pagination tests. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to kill duplication between `articles/views._build_feed` and the profile view.
8	- **htmx.py** — `is_htmx(request) -> bool`. Checks the `HX-Request` header. Used in every view that returns a partial template for HTMX requests and a full template otherwise.
9	- **exceptions.py** — `ResourceNotFound`, `get_or_404`, and `clean_integrity_error`. The last one parses database driver error messages (SQLite and psycopg2) to extract which unique constraint was violated, for converting `IntegrityError` into a nice form error. Tests cover both drivers.
10	- **context_processors.py** — `conduit_context(request)` provides `conduit_user_json` and `conduit_authenticated` to every template. Registered in `config/settings.py::TEMPLATES`.
11	- **tests.py** — unit tests for the above. Uses `unittest.TestCase` for pure functions (no DB), `django.test.TestCase` for database-backed ones.
12	
13	## Patterns to preserve
14	
15	- **No reverse dependencies.** `helpers/` must not import from `apps/`. If something in helpers needs an app-level type, parameterize it or move it to the relevant app. This keeps the module usable from anywhere without cycles.
16	- **`paginate()` is queryset-generic.** When adding a new paginated page, import `paginate` and pass your queryset — don't write offset math inline.
17	- **No `# type: ignore`.** Type issues get fixed at the source. The `clean_integrity_error` function, for example, binds `cause = error.__cause__` to a local so `ty` can narrow through `isinstance` checks (see commit `16fd1d3`).
18	- **`is_htmx` check at the bottom of the view**, not at the top — build the full context first, then pick which template to render. This keeps the full-page and HTMX-partial code paths identical.

---just recipes---
set shell := ["bash", "-uc"]

# Show all available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install dependencies and setup development environment
dev-install:
    make sync
    npm install --silent  # node tooling: specdrive (L3 spec audit), Playwright

# Format code (auto-fix)
format:
    uv run ruff format .

# Lint code (auto-fix, complexity threshold=10)
lint:
    make lint

# Type check code
typecheck:
    make type-check

# Run unit tests
test:
    make test-django-fast

# Run unit tests with coverage threshold (96%)
coverage:
    DEBUG=True DATABASE_URL="file:memdb1?mode=memory&cache=shared" USE_FAST_HASHER=True uv run --with coverage coverage run -m manage test apps helpers
    uv run --with coverage coverage report --fail-under=96
    uv run --with coverage coverage html
    @echo "📊 HTML report: htmlcov/index.html"

# Run integration tests with coverage report (no threshold)
integration-test:
    npm install --silent
    npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
    cd playwright && npx playwright test

# Detailed complexity report for refactoring decisions
complexity:
    uv run --with radon radon cc apps helpers config -a -s --no-assert

# Show N largest files by lines of code
loc N="20":
    cloc apps helpers config --by-file --quiet | head -n $(({{N}} + 5))

# Install FFFlow git hooks (pre-commit framework, delegates to justfile recipes)
hooks-install:
    @if command -v pre-commit >/dev/null; then \
        pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push; \
    else \
        echo "pre-commit not found — install it (uv tool install pre-commit) then re-run."; \
        exit 1; \
    fi

# Validate spec RIDs: format, uniqueness, context-match (FFFlow L3, blocking)
spec-audit:
    npx specdrive audit

# Show declared specs and RID counts
spec-status:
    npx specdrive status

# Cross-reference every spec RID against a test that exercises it (blocking).
# Runs both suites — the Django suite (manage.py test) and the pytest-bdd
# property suite — emits a JUnit report from each, injects each test's RID(s)
# from docs/specs/rid_map.*.yaml, merges the reports, and runs specdrive verify.
spec-verify:
    rm -rf test-reports
    mkdir -p test-reports
    # 0. Merge the per-context rid maps (single source of truth) into one.
    uv run --with pyyaml python scripts/merge_rid_maps.py test-reports/rid_map.django.yaml docs/specs/rid_map.accounts.yaml docs/specs/rid_map.articles.yaml docs/specs/rid_map.comments.yaml docs/specs/rid_map.helpers.yaml
    # 1. Django suite -> JUnit, inject RIDs from the merged map
    DEBUG=True DATABASE_URL="file:memdb1?mode=memory&cache=shared" USE_FAST_HASHER=True \
        TEST_OUTPUT_DIR=test-reports \
        uv run python manage.py test apps helpers
    uv run --with pyyaml python scripts/inject_rids.py test-reports/junit.xml test-reports/rid_map.django.yaml
    # 2. pytest property suite -> JUnit, inject property RIDs
    DEBUG=True DATABASE_URL="file:memdb1?mode=memory&cache=shared" USE_FAST_HASHER=True \
        uv run pytest specs/property/ --junitxml=test-reports/property.xml -q
    uv run --with pyyaml python scripts/inject_rids.py test-reports/property.xml docs/specs/rid_map.property.yaml
    # 3. merge both reports and verify full traceability
    uv run python scripts/merge_junit.py test-reports/merged.xml test-reports/junit.xml test-reports/property.xml
    npx specdrive verify test-reports/merged.xml

# Run all quality checks (format, lint, typecheck, coverage, spec-audit, spec-verify)
check-all: format lint typecheck coverage spec-audit spec-verify
    @echo "✅ All checks passed"

# Remove generated files and artifacts
clean:
    find . -type d -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +
    rm -rf .pytest_cache .hypothesis .coverage htmlcov .ruff_cache test-reports

1	# Behavioral specs (FFFlow L3)
2	
3	These Gherkin feature files are the **behavioral contract** for the app — what
4	it does, in present tense, in domain language. They were extracted from the
5	existing code by FFFlow's `characterize` step, so they describe current
6	behavior (characterization), not aspirations.
7	
8	## Layout
9	
10	One directory per bounded context (matching the Django apps + shared helpers):
11	
12	```
13	docs/specs/
14	  accounts/    authentication, profiles & following, user model
15	  articles/    feeds, authoring, article model, markdown
16	  comments/    commenting, comment model
17	  helpers/     pagination, integrity-error classification, htmx detection
18	```
19	
20	Acceptance specs live at a context root; domain/property specs live under
21	`<context>/domain/`. `*-properties.feature` files hold universal invariants
22	(tagged `@property-based`) suited to property-based testing with Hypothesis.
23	
24	## RIDs (requirement IDs)
25	
26	Every scenario carries a unique `@RID-{CONTEXT}-{NAME}-{NNN}` tag. The CONTEXT
27	segment matches the first directory under `docs/specs/`. These are the anchor
28	points for traceability: spec → test → code.
29	
30	131 scenarios, 131 RIDs.
31	
32	## Gates (both blocking, part of `just check-all`)
33	
34	- **`just spec-audit`** — `specdrive audit`: every RID is well-formed, unique,
35	  and its CONTEXT matches its directory.
36	- **`just spec-verify`** — full spec→test traceability. Runs both test suites,
37	  emits a JUnit report from each, injects each test's RID(s), merges the
38	  reports, and runs `specdrive verify` with `strictTraceability` on.
39	  **131/131 RIDs covered, 0 uncovered.**
40	
41	## How a test declares the scenario it covers
42	
43	`specdrive verify` reads RIDs from the JUnit report as
44	`<property name="rid" value="RID-...">` inside each `<testcase>`. The Django
45	runner doesn't emit per-test properties, so the mapping lives in
46	`docs/specs/rid_map.*.yaml` (`"<classname>::<test_method>": [RID-...]`) and
47	`scripts/inject_rids.py` writes the properties into the report. 15 tests are
48	deliberately unmapped (`@NOSPEC`) — seed/CLI commands and bare GET-render
49	smoke tests with no behavioral scenario.
50	
51	## Two test suites
52	
53	- **Django suite** (`apps/*/tests.py`, `helpers/tests.py`, `manage.py test`) —
54	  the 124 example/behavioral tests, including `hypothesis.extra.django`
55	  property tests for DB-backed invariants (slug stability, email-identity,
56	  self-follow).
57	- **Property suite** (`specs/property/`, pytest + `pytest-bdd-property`) — binds
58	  the DB-free `@property-based` pagination scenarios directly to the Gherkin
59	  feature file; Hypothesis generates 100+ inputs per scenario.
60	
61	## `@unverified-intent`
62	
63	Seven scenarios carry a `# @unverified-intent:` comment. These pin behavior
64	that is *currently* true but may be an unintended quirk (e.g. a self-follow is a
65	silent no-op; an out-of-range page number echoes back rather than clamping).
66	They are documented as the contract and flagged for stakeholder review — not
67	silently "fixed."

1	from dataclasses import dataclass
2	
3	from django.db.models import QuerySet
4	from django.http import HttpRequest
5	
6	DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 10
7	
8	
9	@dataclass
10	class Page:
11	    items: list
12	    page: int
13	    pages: range
14	
15	
16	def paginate(
17	    queryset: QuerySet,
18	    request: HttpRequest,
19	    per_page: int = DEFAULT_PER_PAGE,
20	) -> Page:
21	    """Paginate queryset by ?page= query param.
22	
23	    Invalid / missing / non-positive page defaults to 1, matching the
24	    behavior the e2e suite relies on (commit 48d39f8). Django's built-in
25	    Paginator raises on invalid input and is deliberately not used here.
26	    """
27	    try:
28	        page = int(request.GET.get("page", 1))
29	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
30	        page = 1
31	    page = max(1, page)
32	    offset = (page - 1) * per_page
33	    total = queryset.count()
34	    items = list(queryset[offset : offset + per_page])
35	    total_pages = max(1, (total + per_page - 1) // per_page)
36	    return Page(items=items, page=page, pages=range(1, total_pages + 1))

# apps/

Three Django apps, one per domain. Kept deliberately thin and layered.

## Apps

- **accounts** — users, auth, profile pages. Custom `User` model extending `AbstractUser`, email-as-username.
- **articles** — articles, feeds, tags, favorites. Owns `profile_view` since profiles are mostly article lists.
- **comments** — article comments. Depends on articles; nothing depends on comments.

## Layering

Import direction is **one-way**: `accounts → articles`, `comments → articles`. Nothing imports from `accounts` into the others. `articles` is the center; `comments` and `accounts` wrap it.

This is deliberate. The layering violation where `accounts/views.py` imported `Article` was fixed in the `refactor-pass` epic by moving the profile-view body into `articles/views.py` while keeping the URL routed through `accounts/urls.py`.

## sys.path note

`config/settings.py` adds `apps/` to `sys.path`, so imports inside these apps look like `from articles.models import Article` — **not** `from apps.articles.models import Article`. This is load-bearing for tests, URL routing, and the Django app registry. If you see a tool (mypy, pyright, editor) complain about unresolved imports, that's why; `ty` is configured to ignore `unresolved-import` in `pyproject.toml`.
=====CONFIG=====
# config/

Django project configuration: settings, URL conf, WSGI/ASGI entry points.

## Key components

- **settings.py** — the single settings module. Reads env vars at import time.
- **urls.py** — top-level URL conf. Includes each app's `urls.py`; no API routes (no `/api/*`).
- **wsgi.py** / **asgi.py** — standard Django deployment entry points.

## Non-obvious things about settings.py

- **`apps/` is injected into `sys.path`** at line 16. This is what makes `from accounts.models import User` work across the codebase. If you move files around, this line is load-bearing.
- **Database selection is env-var driven with three modes:**
  1. `DATABASE_URL` starts with `:memory:` or `file:` → in-memory SQLite (used by unit tests and Playwright webServer)
  2. `DATABASE_URL` set otherwise → parsed as PostgreSQL
  3. `DEBUG=True` with no `DATABASE_URL` → file-based SQLite (`db.sqlite3` in repo root)
  4. Anything else → `raise SystemExit` with a helpful error
- **`USE_FAST_HASHER=True`** switches to `MD5PasswordHasher` for test speed. Only allowed with `DEBUG=True` (raises otherwise). This is why `just test-django-fast` runs in ~0.4s.
- **`AUTH_USER_MODEL = "accounts.User"`** — custom user model. Any new foreign key to users should use `settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL`, not `from accounts.models import User` directly (prevents circular import risks).
- **Environment branches have `# pragma: no cover`** on the Postgres, raise-on-misconfig, and file-SQLite-default lines. These aren't exercised by the test runner but are exercised in real deployment — not dead code, just untestable under our test env.

## Template context processors

`helpers.context_processors.conduit_context` is registered — it exposes `conduit_user_json` and `conduit_authenticated` to every template. Used by `templates/base.html` to set `window.__conduit_debug__` for browser-console debugging.

1	# playwright/
2	
3	Playwright e2e test harness. Runs the shared RealWorld spec against this implementation.
4	
5	## Files
6	
7	- **playwright.config.ts** — the whole config. Points at `realworld/specs/e2e` (vendored upstream spec) for test files, auto-starts a Django dev server via the `webServer` block, runs in a single worker (no parallelism).
8	
9	## How it runs
10	
11	1. `just integration-test` runs `cd playwright && npx playwright test` (or `API_MODE=false npx playwright test` directly)
12	2. Playwright's `webServer` block starts Django with `DEBUG=True`, in-memory SQLite (`file:memdb1?mode=memory&cache=shared`), `USE_FAST_HASHER=True`. It runs migrations, then `seed_data`, then `runserver --noreload` on port 8000.
13	3. Tests hit `http://localhost:8000` via the browser. Each test manages its own user via the register flow.
14	4. When Playwright exits, the dev server is torn down.
15	
16	## API_MODE and skipped tests
17	
18	The RealWorld e2e suite is shared across implementations, including API-based ones. ~65 tests are API-only (they hit `/api/user`, `/api/articles`, etc., which this implementation does not have). They gate themselves with `test.skip(!API_MODE, ...)` at the top of each test, so passing `API_MODE=false` (the default here) causes them to self-skip rather than fail.
19	
20	**Expected baseline**: 74 passed, 65 skipped, 0 failed. Deviations from this are the test signal — if the passed count drops, a regression was introduced; if the failed count goes up, investigate first (the spec sometimes drifts when the vendored upstream copy is refreshed).
21	
22	## Why npx and not bun
23	
24	The original `make e2e` target uses `bun` per upstream, but we don't ship bun in all environments. `just integration-test` uses `npx playwright test` instead — same tests, same config, no bun dependency. Both paths work.
25	
26	## Test artifacts
27	
28	- `test-results/` — failure screenshots, videos, traces. Regenerated every run; in `.gitignore`.
29	- `playwright-report/` — HTML report. Regenerated every run; in `.gitignore`.
30	- `node_modules/` — `@playwright/test` and its deps. In `.gitignore`.
31	
32	## Never modify test files from here
33	
34	The specs live in `realworld/specs/e2e/*.spec.ts` (vendored upstream content). That's upstream content. If a test is wrong for this implementation, fix it upstream or filter it via `API_MODE` — don't edit the vendored copy directly.

---config.yaml---
version: 1
level: L3
stack: python
capture: github-issues
spec_location: docs/specs
# Django convention: tests live per-app as apps/*/tests.py, plus helpers/tests.py.
# There is no central tests/ directory.
test_location: apps
audit_state_file: .ffflow/audit.yaml

# NOTE: the python stack cartridge declares max_level: L2 on the assumption that
# specdrive is npm-only and therefore Python-incompatible. That is a packaging
# assumption, not a capability limit: specdrive is a language-agnostic CLI
# (github:bryonjacob/specdrive) that consumes JUnit XML, so it works fine against
# a Django suite. This project runs at L3 deliberately, overriding that cap.
features:
  property_based_testing: true
  mutation_testing: true
  rid_traceability: true
  four_quality_gates: true

inject_rids.py

2	
3	Binds the @property-based PAGINATION-* scenarios in
4	docs/specs/articles/domain/article-properties.feature to Hypothesis via
5	pytest-bdd-property. They exercise helpers.pagination.paginate directly — the

10	"""
11	
12	from django.test import RequestFactory
13	from hypothesis import strategies as st
14	from pytest_bdd import scenario
15	from pytest_bdd_property import property_then, property_when, register_strategy
16	
17	from helpers.pagination import DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, paginate
18	
19	_rf = RequestFactory()
20	
21	_FEATURE = "../../docs/specs/articles/domain/article-properties.feature"
22	
23	# Bind only the DB-free pagination properties by name. SLUG-003 in the same
24	# feature file is DB-backed and covered by a hypothesis.extra.django test in the
25	# Django suite, so it is deliberately NOT collected here (binding it with no
26	# steps would pass vacuously).
27	
28	
29	@scenario(_FEATURE, "Any page request resolves to a page of one or more")
30	def test_pagination_003():
31	    pass
32	
33	
34	@scenario(_FEATURE, "A page never holds more articles than the page size")
35	def test_pagination_004():
36	    pass
37	
38	
39	@scenario(_FEATURE, "The reported page range always contains at least one page")
40	def test_pagination_005():
41	    pass
42	
43	
44	class _FakeQuerySet:
45	    """List-backed queryset supporting the slice + count paginate() needs."""
46	
47	    def __init__(self, n: int):
48	        self._items = list(range(n))
49	
50	    def count(self) -> int:
51	        return len(self._items)
52	
53	    def __getitem__(self, s):
54	        return self._items[s]
55	
56	
57	# "any article collection <C>" -> 0..50 articles. Includes the empty collection,
58	# which is what PAGINATION-005 ("including none at all") relies on.
59	register_strategy("article collection", lambda: st.integers(min_value=0, max_value=50).map(_FakeQuerySet))
60	# "any page number <N>" -> arbitrary int, including out-of-range and negatives.
61	register_strategy("page number", lambda: st.integers(min_value=-5, max_value=60))

1	Feature: Pagination invariants
2	  As a developer relying on the paginator across many call sites
3	  I want the paginator to uphold the same guarantees for every possible input
4	  So that views and templates can trust its output without defensive checks.
5	
6	  These are universal properties that hold for any queryset and any ?page=
7	  value, derived from the slicing and clamping logic in paginate().
8	
9	  Rule: The reported page is always a positive integer
10	
11	    @property-based @RID-HELPERS-PAGINATE-PROP-001
12	    Scenario Outline: Any page input yields a reported page of at least 1
13	      Given a queryset of <total> records
14	      When the developer paginates with page "<input>" at <per_page> per page
15	      Then the reported page is at least 1
16	
17	      Examples:
18	        | total | input | per_page |
19	        | 25    | 2     | 10       |
20	        | 25    | abc   | 10       |
21	        | 25    | 0     | 10       |
22	        | 25    | -5    | 10       |
23	        | 0     |       | 10       |
24	        | 5     | 99    | 10       |
25	
26	  Rule: A page never holds more records than the per-page window
27	
28	    @property-based @RID-HELPERS-PAGINATE-PROP-002
29	    Scenario Outline: The returned record count never exceeds per_page
30	      Given a queryset of <total> records
31	      When the developer paginates with page "<input>" at <per_page> per page
32	      Then the page holds at most <per_page> records
33	
34	      Examples:
35	        | total | input | per_page |
36	        | 25    | 1     | 10       |
37	        | 25    | 3     | 10       |
38	        | 25    | 99    | 10       |
39	        | 3     | 1     | 10       |
40	        | 0     | 1     | 10       |
41	        | 25    | 1     | 5        |
42	
43	  Rule: The page range always begins at 1 and spans at least one page
44	
45	    @property-based @RID-HELPERS-PAGINATE-PROP-003
46	    Scenario Outline: The page range is 1-based and never empty
47	      Given a queryset of <total> records
48	      When the developer paginates with page "<input>" at <per_page> per page
49	      Then the page range starts at 1
50	      And the page range spans at least one page
51	      And the page range covers ceil(total / per_page) pages, but never fewer than one
52	
53	      Examples:
54	        | total | input | per_page |
55	        | 25    | 1     | 10       |
56	        | 0     | 1     | 10       |
57	        | 5     | 99    | 10       |
58	        | 10    | 1     | 10       |

===CLAUDE.md root===
# realworld-django-htmx
**Django + HTMX fullstack implementation of the RealWorld spec — no API, no SPA**

## About this codebase

This is a fullstack RealWorld (Medium clone) implementation that has been set up
to use the **FFFlow plugin** — an opinionated, prescriptive development workflow
(plan → work → audit) for Claude Code. The repo's specs, tests, and quality
gates are organized around that workflow.

Whenever you're doing development or feature work here, first check whether the
FFFlow plugin is installed (look for `/fff:` commands, or run `/plugin`). If it
is not installed, encourage the user to install it and give them these exact
commands to run inside Claude Code:

    /plugin marketplace add bryonjacob/ffflow
    /plugin install fff@ffflow
    /reload-plugins

Once installed, use the FFFlow workflow for the work at hand.

## Rules

- **NEVER raise timeouts** without asking first. We build fast software. If a test times out, the code is broken — fix the code, don't raise the timeout. Raising timeouts destroys the feedback loop.
- **NEVER use `# type: ignore`**. Fix type issues at the source. If `ty` complains, the fix is in the code (narrow with an `isinstance`, bind a local, use a concrete type) — not in a suppression comment.
- **NEVER rename form field names** (`email`, `password`, `title`, `description`, `body`, etc.) or visible text labels (`Sign in`, `Your Feed`, `Publish Article`, etc.) without checking `realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md`. The e2e suite pins these.

## Before finishing

Run `just check-all` (lint + type-check + unit tests + 100% coverage gate). Optionally run `just integration-test` for the full Playwright e2e suite (baseline: 74 passed, 65 skipped, 0 failed).

## Testing

When asked to "run the tests", run both `just check-all` and `just integration-test`. Unit tests live per-app (`apps/*/tests.py`) plus `helpers/tests.py`, covering views, models, forms, and helpers via `django.test.Client`. E2e tests are the shared RealWorld spec (vendored at `realworld/specs/e2e/`) driven by Playwright.

- **Unit tests**: fast, ~0.5s, in-memory SQLite + MD5 hasher, 100% coverage.
- **E2e tests**: slower, ~2.5min, real browser against a spawned Django dev server.

Both need to pass before a change is done.

## Commands

Primary tooling is `just` (see `justfile`). Legacy `make` targets still work and are delegated to by some `just` recipes.

- `just dev-install` — install deps (`uv sync --extra dev`)
- `just check-all` — format, lint, typecheck, coverage (enforced 96% floor, actual 100%)
- `just test` — unit tests only (fast)
- `just coverage` — unit tests + coverage report (HTML at `htmlcov/index.html`)
- `just lint` / `just format` / `just typecheck` — individual gates
- `just integration-test` — Playwright e2e suite (auto-starts Django webServer)
- `just complexity` — radon complexity report
- `just loc` — largest files by LOC
- `just clean` — remove caches and coverage artifacts

Running the server:

- `DEBUG=True make run-debug` — dev server on http://localhost:8000
- `DEBUG=True make migrate` — apply migrations

## Per-module docs

There's a `CLAUDE.md` in every meaningful module:

- `apps/CLAUDE.md` — app layering rules, `sys.path` note
- `apps/accounts/CLAUDE.md`, `apps/articles/CLAUDE.md`, `apps/comments/CLAUDE.md` — per-app purpose, components, gotchas
- `config/CLAUDE.md` — Django settings, env-var database selection, `# pragma` branches
- `helpers/CLAUDE.md` — shared utilities (`paginate`, `is_htmx`, `clean_integrity_error`)
- `templates/CLAUDE.md` — full-page vs partial split, selectors contract
- `playwright/CLAUDE.md` — e2e harness, API_MODE, baseline

Base directory for this skill: /home/claude/working/ffflow-plugin/plugin/skills/plan-chat

# plan-chat

## Plan Mode

This skill does NOT invoke Plan Mode. Claude Code's Plan Mode and FFFlow plans are different things — this skill creates an FFFlow plan on disk by writing files and confirming with the user, not by entering Plan Mode.

## Purpose

Stand up a working plan directory for one change. By the end of the session there is a sealed `<plan-dir>/plan.md` describing the path from current to target spec, plus a `decisions.md` capturing every choice made — with **zero open `?` markers**.

## When to invoke

- A new behavior change is about to start.
- Useful at every level. The artifact format changes with level; the workflow doesn't.

## Inputs

- A description of the change (free-form, from the user).
- `.ffflow/config.yaml` — read for level, stack, capture backend.

## Outputs

Where `<plan-dir>` = `/tmp/ffflow-plans/<project-hash>/<slug>/` (project-hash from `sha256(pwd) | head -c 16`, same convention as `notetoself`).

- `<plan-dir>/plan.md` — the plan itself.
- `<plan-dir>/decisions.md` — every decision made + rejected alternatives. Zero open `?` markers when sealed.
- `<plan-dir>/chat-log.md` — optional running transcript for archaeology.
- `<plan-dir>/metadata.json` — slug, phase, created date, level.
- Optionally a draft spec delta (`<plan-dir>/spec-delta.md`) showing the proposed spec change.

## Dependencies

- Level-appropriate methodology skills, loaded as reference context:
  - L1+: `hexagonal-architecture`, `defect-driven-specification`.
  - L2+: `writing-specs`, `spec-first-development`, `contract-enforcement`.
  - L3: `rid-traceability`, `total-specification`, `quality-gates`.

## Flow

### 0. Setup

1. Read `.ffflow/config.yaml`. If absent, prompt the user to run `/init-ffflow` first and stop.
2. Ask for a short kebab-case slug for the plan (e.g. `auth-token-refresh`).
3. Create `<plan-dir>/`. If one already exists for this slug, offer to resume rather than overwrite.
4. Write a skeleton `plan.md` with the three phase headings and the slug + level recorded at the top.
5. Write `metadata.json` with `phase: chat-incomplete`.

### 1. Understanding

Clarify scope. Ask sharp questions early.

- What problem does this solve? Who benefits?
- What does the current evergreen spec say about this area? Read it before asking the user.
- What exists in the code? Scan for related modules / ports / adapters / spec entries.
- What's out of scope? Mark explicitly.
- What constraints apply? Performance, security, compatibility, deadline.

Do not move on until the user confirms the problem statement. Write the confirmed problem statement into `plan.md` Phase 1.

### 2. Architecture / Approach

Design the path through the code.

- **L0**: prose. "We'll add X to module Y. The contract is: input A → output B." That's enough.
- **L1**: prose + hexagonal layer mapping. Which port? Which adapter? Where does the new code sit?
- **L2**: prose + draft Gherkin Rules + Scenarios. Tag `@property-based` candidates. Identify spec types per layer.
- **L3**: above, plus draft RIDs (`@RID-XXX` placeholders), mutation-testing scope, contract enforcement plan.

Surface decisions as you go. Open ones use `?` markers in `decisions.md`:

```
? Should token refresh happen on every request or only when expiring < 5 min?
```

Write decisions to `decisions.md` continuously as conversation proceeds. Don't batch them at the end.

### 3. Path

Describe the change as a sequence of steps that will become tasks. This is not the same as `plan-breakdown` (which decomposes into independent chess moves), but it does the rough cut.

- Which parts of the spec change, in what order?
- What depends on what?
- Where are the natural commit boundaries?

Write to Phase 3 of `plan.md`.

### 4. Resolve every open decision

**This skill does not seal until every `?` marker in `decisions.md` is resolved.** No exceptions.

For each open `?`:

1. **Restate the question** in plain language. Don't dump the `?` block back; rephrase.
2. **Present 2–3 alternatives**, each with:
   - A concrete name.
   - A one-line tradeoff (cost vs. benefit).
   - Implications for spec, implementation, or downstream work.
   Use evidence where available — file references, similar past decisions, prior plans in `/tmp/ffflow-plans/<project-hash>/`.
3. **Name a recommendation.** Don't be neutral. The user can override; abstaining wastes their time.
4. **Ask for confirmation.** Either "go with X" or "different — tell me which."
5. **Record the answer** in `decisions.md` with rejected alternatives:

   ```
   ✓ Token refresh strategy
      Chose: threshold-based (refresh when < 5min remaining)
      Rationale: balances network overhead against the auth-failure cliff for users on slow networks.
      Rejected alternatives:
        - every request: too much network traffic
        - on 401 retry: too much latency for unhappy paths
   ```

6. If the decision changes content in Phase 2 or Phase 3 of `plan.md`, update those sections — don't strand stale text.

If the user wants to **defer** a decision, write `? (deferred): <reason>` and continue. The skill will still refuse to seal — `plan-breakdown` requires zero opens.

### 5. Seal

Plan is sealed when:

- Zero open `?` markers in `decisions.md` (deferred markers count as open).
- User confirms "ready to break this down."

Update `metadata.json`:
```json
{
  "phase": "chat-complete",
  "ready_for_breakdown": true
}
```

Print:
```
✓ <plan-dir>/ sealed (chat-complete)
Next: /plan-breakdown
```

## Resume

Re-running `plan-chat` against an existing plan directory:
1. Read `metadata.json`. If `phase: chat-complete` and user is starting a new direction, refuse — they should start a new plan slug, or revert the metadata explicitly.
2. Otherwise, read `plan.md` and `decisions.md`. If any `?` markers exist, jump to step 4 (resolve every open decision). Otherwise, pick up at the latest unfinished phase.

## Friction addressed

- Plan Mode misfires (200+ turn chats inside Plan Mode that should have been writing to disk).
- Bloated chats that lose context after `/clear`. Plan files persist.
- Hand-pasted "walk me through alternatives" templates — now part of the chat's discipline.
- Plans that "seal" with open questions, then surprise everyone at breakdown time.
- Specs falling behind — plan optionally writes a spec-delta to commit alongside the work.

## Anti-patterns

- Don't write final RIDs here. Placeholders only — RIDs assigned at capture.
- Don't decompose into tasks here — that's `plan-breakdown`'s job.
- Don't try to do all three phases in one turn. Confirm each phase with the user.
- Don't write code. Plans describe intent.
- Don't seal with open `?`s. The discipline is what makes breakdown clean.
- Don't recommend "it depends" — pick something.
- Don't lose rejected alternatives. Future archaeology needs them.

## Quality checks before sealing

- [ ] Problem statement recorded in `plan.md` Phase 1, confirmed by user.
- [ ] Architecture/approach written in Phase 2, with level-appropriate detail.
- [ ] Path written in Phase 3.
- [ ] `decisions.md` has zero open `?` markers (including deferred).
- [ ] `metadata.json` shows `chat-complete`.
- [ ] At L2+, draft Gherkin parses if any was written.

1	# scripts/
2	
3	Small helper scripts for the L3 spec→test traceability pipeline. They are
4	invoked by the `spec-verify` recipe in the `justfile`; they are not part of the
5	application and are not imported by it.
6	
7	## Files
8	
9	- **inject_rids.py** — injects specdrive RID `<property>` elements into a JUnit
10	  XML report, mapping each test to the scenario RID(s) it covers (from the
11	  `docs/specs/rid_map.*.yaml` files). The Django test runner can't emit per-test
12	  properties, so this post-processes the report.
13	- **merge_junit.py** — merges multiple JUnit XML reports into one
14	  `<testsuites>` document. `specdrive verify` reads a single report, but the
15	  project produces two suites (Django + pytest property suite).
16	- **merge_rid_maps.py** — merges the per-context `docs/specs/rid_map.<context>.yaml`
17	  files (the single source of truth, one per bounded context) into the combined
18	  map `inject_rids.py` consumes, so the combined map is never a committed,
19	  drift-prone artifact.
20	
21	## How they fit together
22	
23	`just spec-verify` runs both test suites → emits a JUnit report from each →
24	`inject_rids.py` stamps RIDs into each from the merged map → `merge_junit.py`
25	combines them → `specdrive verify` cross-references RIDs against the specs.
26

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Inject specdrive RID <property> elements into a JUnit XML report.
3	
4	specdrive verify reads RIDs from each <testcase> via
5	`<property name="rid" value="RID-...">`. unittest-xml-reporting emits only
6	testsuite-level properties, so this post-processor adds per-testcase rid
7	properties from a mapping file.
8	
9	Mapping file (docs/specs/rid_map.yaml) is the single source of truth:
10	    "<classname>::<test_name>": [RID-..., RID-...]
11	A test mapped to an empty list / "@NOSPEC" is treated as deliberately unspecced.
12	
13	Usage: inject_rids.py <junit.xml> <rid_map.yaml>
14	"""
15	
16	import sys
17	import xml.dom.minidom as minidom
18	from pathlib import Path
19	
20	import yaml
21	
22	
23	def main() -> int:
24	    report_path, map_path = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
25	    rid_map = yaml.safe_load(map_path.read_text()) or {}
26	
27	    doc = minidom.parse(str(report_path))
28	    injected = 0
29	    unmapped: list[str] = []
30	
31	    for tc in doc.getElementsByTagName("testcase"):
32	        name = tc.getAttribute("name")
33	        key = f"{tc.getAttribute('classname')}::{name}"
34	        rids = rid_map.get(key)
35	        # pytest parametrized cases carry a [param] suffix; one map entry per
36	        # base scenario covers all its examples.
37	        if rids is None and "[" in name:
38	            base = f"{tc.getAttribute('classname')}::{name.split('[', 1)[0]}"
39	            rids = rid_map.get(base)
40	        if rids is None:
41	            unmapped.append(key)
42	            continue
43	        if isinstance(rids, str):
44	            rids = [rids]
45	        props = doc.createElement("properties")
46	        for rid in rids:
47	            p = doc.createElement("property")
48	            p.setAttribute("name", "rid")
49	            p.setAttribute("value", rid)
50	            props.appendChild(p)
51	        tc.insertBefore(props, tc.firstChild)
52	        injected += 1
53	
54	    report_path.write_text(doc.toxml())
55	    print(f"injected rid properties into {injected} testcase(s)")
56	    if unmapped:
57	        print(f"WARNING: {len(unmapped)} testcase(s) absent from {map_path.name}:")
58	        for k in unmapped:
59	            print(f"  - {k}")
60	        return 1
61	    return 0
62	
63	
64	if __name__ == "__main__":
65	    raise SystemExit(main())
66

===== apps/accounts/CLAUDE.md =====
# apps/accounts

User model, auth views, profile routing.

## Purpose

Owns the custom `User` model, the login/register/settings/logout flows, and the URL routing for `/profile/<username>` (the actual profile rendering logic lives in `apps/articles/views.py::profile_view` — this app just keeps the URLs and the delegating shims).

## Key components

- **models.py** — `User(AbstractUser)` with email as the `USERNAME_FIELD`, plus a self-referential M2M `followers`. Has `is_following(other_user)` for template checks. `UserManager` overrides `create_user` / `create_superuser`.
- **views.py** — `login_view`, `register_view`, `settings_view`, `logout_view`, `follow_view`, plus two thin `profile_view` / `profile_favorites_view` shims that delegate to `articles.views.profile_view`.
- **forms.py** — `LoginForm`, `RegisterForm`, `SettingsForm` (a `ModelForm`). Field names must match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract — **don't rename them**.
- **urls.py** — `/login`, `/register`, `/settings`, `/logout`, `/profile/<username>`, `/profile/<username>/favorites`, `/profile/<username>/follow`.

## Non-obvious things

- `User.USERNAME_FIELD = "email"` — auth uses email, not the username field, for login. `username` is a display/URL handle only.
- `create_user` sets an unusable password if none given. Used by `seed_data` management command.
- `follow_view` is HTMX-aware: returns a partial if `HX-Request` header is set, otherwise redirects. Same pattern throughout the project.
- The `accounts/profile_404.html` template is used when a profile URL hits a missing user — intentional custom 404, not Django's default.
- Do **not** re-introduce `from articles.models import Article` here. That was the layering violation we fixed in the `refactor-pass` epic (see repo root CLAUDE.md).

## Dependencies

- **Uses**: `articles.views.profile_view` (thin shim only; no model imports), `helpers.exceptions`, `helpers.htmx`.
- **Used by**: nothing (accounts is a leaf — other apps import `User` via `get_user_model()` / `settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL`, not directly).

===== apps/articles/CLAUDE.md =====
# apps/articles

Articles, feeds, tags, favorites, and the profile-page renderer.

## Purpose

The core content app. Owns everything about articles themselves (model, CRUD views, feed composition, tag handling, favorites) and — after the `refactor-pass` epic — also owns the profile-page view body because profiles are mostly article lists.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Article` model plus an `ArticleQuerySet` with `with_favorites(user)` that annotates each row with `num_favorites` and `is_favorite`. Slug is auto-generated once on create via `Article.save()` and **stable on edit** (per commit `ae3c5ed`).
- **views.py** — the biggest view file in the project. Contains:
  - `home_view` / `tag_view` — both delegate to `_build_feed(request, tag=...)`
  - `_build_feed` — orchestrator: parses `?feed=`/`?page=`, calls `_feed_queryset`, redirects anonymous users away from the following feed, paginates, caches tags, picks template (full page vs HTMX partial)
  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. Returns `(None, "following")` when anonymous users request the following feed (caller redirects to login). Single extraction point for new feed types (drafts, bookmarks, search).
  - `article_detail_view`, `article_create_view`, `article_edit_view`, `article_delete_view`, `article_favorite_view`
  - `_save_article_form(form, article)` — private helper that translates form field names (`description`, `body`) to model field names (`summary`, `content`). **Don't rename either side** — form names are pinned by the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
  - `profile_view(request, username, tab)` — the actual profile page renderer. Called by shims in `accounts/views.py`. Handles "my articles" and "favorites" tabs with per-tab querysets.
- **constants.py** — `ARTICLES_PER_PAGE`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`, `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`. Introduced in the `refactor-pass` epic to replace magic values.
- **forms.py** — `ArticleForm` with fields `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags`. Field names match the RealWorld SELECTORS.md contract.
- **admin.py** — auto-registers every model in the project via `apps.get_models()`. Lives here for historical reasons — code smell but harmless.
- **management/commands/seed_data.py** — creates `johndoe` / `janedoe` users and 8 articles. Used by Playwright's `webServer` block.
- **templatetags/markdown_filter.py** — `render_markdown` filter that sanitizes via `nh3.clean()`. Used in article detail pages.

## Non-obvious things

- Feed selection logic lives in `_feed_queryset`. If you're adding a new feed type (drafts, search, bookmarks), that's the one function to extend — everything downstream (pagination, HTMX partials, template) flows from its return value.
- The tag list is cached for 5 minutes under `ALL_TAGS_CACHE_KEY`. `_save_article_form` invalidates the cache on article save so new tags show up immediately on the home page.
- `_build_feed` redirects to `/login` when an anonymous user passes `?feed=following`. This is a server-side redirect, not a template guard.
- HTMX requests get `partials/feed_content.html` instead of `articles/home.html`. The partial is a fragment of the same feed UI; full-page loads and HTMX tab-swaps both render the same feed code path.
- `Article.save()` regenerates the slug **only if `self.pk is None`** — editing the title of a published article does not change its URL.

## Dependencies

- **Uses**: `helpers.pagination.paginate`, `helpers.htmx.is_htmx`, `taggit` (3rd-party), `markdown` + `nh3` (in templatetag).
- **Used by**: `comments` (imports `Article`), `accounts` (imports only `profile_view`, no model or query access).

===== apps/comments/CLAUDE.md =====
# apps/comments

Article comments. Small app — one model, two views.

## Key components

- **models.py** — `Comment` with ForeignKeys to `Article` and `User`, plus `content`/`created`/`updated` fields. No custom manager.
- **views.py** — `comment_create_view` (POST, trims whitespace, ignores empty bodies) and `comment_delete_view` (POST, allows delete by comment author OR article author, returns 403 for anyone else).
- **urls.py** — `/article/<slug>/comment`, `/article/<slug>/comment/<id>/delete`.

## Non-obvious things

- **Never use `article.comment_set`** — use `Comment.objects.filter(article=article)` instead. Django's reverse-FK accessor `comment_set` isn't typed by `django-types`, and using it triggers `ty` warnings. This was changed in commit `0cb53f4`.
- Both views are HTMX-aware: they return `partials/comment_list.html` on HTMX requests and redirect to the article page on normal form posts.
- Comment deletion by the **article** author (not just the comment author) is a deliberate feature — it's tested in `tests.py::test_article_author_can_delete` and is part of the e2e suite.

  - `_feed_queryset(user, feed, tag) -> (QuerySet | None, str)` — private helper that returns the filtered article queryset + active-tab string. # Django+HTMX RealWorld Codebase — Foundation for a Notifications App

## Critical architecture note (read first)

`config/settings.py:16` injects `apps/` into `sys.path`: `sys.path.insert(0, str(BASE_DIR / "apps"))`. So intra-project imports are `from articles.models import Article`, **not** `from apps.articles.models import Article`. But in `INSTALLED_APPS` the apps are listed with the `apps.` prefix (`"apps.accounts"`, etc.). This dual convention is load-bearing — replicate it exactly for a new app.

Import direction is one-way: `accounts → articles`, `comments → articles`. `articles` is the center. `helpers/` has zero reverse deps. A notifications app would naturally sit at the outer layer (it can import from `accounts`, `articles`, `comments` models), but nothing should import *from* it.

---

## 1. Per-app structure and model definitions

Every app has the same file set: `__init__.py`, `admin.py`, `apps.py`, `models.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py`, `tests.py`, `migrations/`. `accounts` and `articles` additionally have `forms.py`; `comments` has none. `articles` also has `constants.py`, `templatetags/`. Two apps have `management/commands/`.

### accounts — `User` model (`apps/accounts/models.py`)

The custom user IS the profile (no separate Profile model). Email is the login field; `username` is a display/URL handle.

```
# apps/accounts/models.py:29-54
class User(AbstractUser):
    first_name = None
    last_name = None
    email = models.EmailField("Email Address", unique=True)          # :34
    username = models.CharField(max_length=60, unique=True)          # :35
    bio = models.TextField(blank=True)                               # :36
    image = models.URLField(null=True, blank=True)                   # :37
    followers = models.ManyToManyField("self", blank=True, symmetrical=False)  # :39
    EMAIL_FIELD = "email"
    USERNAME_FIELD = "email"
    REQUIRED_FIELDS: list[str] = []
    objects = UserManager()
    ...
    def is_following(self, other_user):                             # :53-54
        return other_user.followers.filter(pk=self.pk).exists() if self.is_authenticated else False
```

**The follow relationship** is the self-referential M2M `User.followers` (`:39`). It is asymmetrical (`symmetrical=False`). Semantics: `X in profile_user.followers` means "X follows profile_user". So `profile_user.followers.add(request.user)` = request.user starts following profile_user. `is_following(other)` checks `other.followers.filter(pk=self.pk)` (`:54`). There is no `related_name`, so the reverse accessor is the auto `user_set` (unused in the codebase).

`UserManager` (`:7-26`) overrides `create_user` (sets unusable password if none given) and `create_superuser`.

### articles — `Article` model (`apps/articles/models.py`)

```
# apps/articles/models.py:26-44
class Article(models.Model):
    author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)  # :27
    title = models.CharField(max_length=150, unique=True, blank=False)              # :28
    summary = models.TextField(blank=True)                                          # :29
    content = models.TextField(blank=True)                                          # :30
    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)                # :32
    updated = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)                                   # :33
    tags = TaggableManager(blank=True)                                              # :35
    favorites = models.ManyToManyField(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, blank=True, related_name="favorites")  # :36
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True, max_length=255)                            # :37
    objects = ArticleManager()
    def save(self, *args, **kwargs):                                                # :41-44
        if not self.pk:
            self.slug = slugify(self.title)
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)
```

**The favorite relationship** is `Article.favorites` M2M to User (`:36`), `related_name="favorites"` so `user.favorites` = articles that user favorited. Note the model uses `settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL` for FKs (not a direct `User` import) — the documented convention for new user FKs.

`ArticleQuerySet.with_favorites(user)` (`:11-20`) annotates `num_favorites` (Count) and `is_favorite` (Exists). `ArticleManager = models.Manager.from_queryset(ArticleQuerySet)` (`:23`).

Note: form field names (`description`, `body`) differ from model field names (`summary`, `content`); mapped in `_save_article_form`.

### comments — `Comment` model (`apps/comments/models.py`)

```
# apps/comments/models.py:6-11
class Comment(models.Model):
    article = models.ForeignKey(Article, on_delete=models.CASCADE)                  # :7
    author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)  # :8
    content = models.TextField()                                                    # :9
    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)                # :10
    updated = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)                                   # :11
```

This app imports the concrete `Article` (`from articles.models import Article`, `:1`) but uses `settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL` for the user FK. No custom manager, no Meta ordering. Convention (per comments/CLAUDE.md): query via `Comment.objects.filter(article=article)`, **not** `article.comment_set` — except note `article_detail_view` in articles actually DOES use `article.comment_set` at `apps/articles/views.py:127`. So both patterns exist; comments' own views use the explicit filter.

### admin.py

`accounts/admin.py` and `comments/admin.py` are empty stubs (just `# Register your models here.`). `articles/admin.py:1-10` is the real one — it auto-registers **every** model project-wide via `apps.get_models()` with an `AlreadyRegistered` guard. So a new Notification model would be auto-registered in admin without touching any admin.py, as long as `articles/admin.py` runs.

### apps.py

All three are identical 3-field AppConfigs. Example (`apps/comments/apps.py:4-6`):
```
class CommentsConfig(AppConfig):
    default_auto_field = "django.db.models.BigAutoField"
    name = "comments"     # note: bare name, NOT "apps.comments"
```
The `name` attribute is the bare app label (`comments`), matching the `sys.path` import convention — even though INSTALLED_APPS uses `apps.comments`.

---

## 2. Exact write sites — follow, favorite, comment

These are the hook points a notification would be triggered from.

### Follow / unfollow — `apps/accounts/views.py:86-108` `follow_view`

`@login_required @require_POST`, keyed by `username`. Toggle:
```
# apps/accounts/views.py:88-98
profile_user = get_object_or_404(User, username=username)
if profile_user != request.user:
    if profile_user.followers.filter(pk=request.user.id).exists():
        profile_user.followers.remove(request.user)   # :92  UNFOLLOW write
        is_following = False
    else:
        profile_user.followers.add(request.user)      # :95  FOLLOW write
        is_following = True
else:
    is_following = False
```
- **Follow created:** `apps/accounts/views.py:95` `profile_user.followers.add(request.user)`
- **Follow reversed:** `apps/accounts/views.py:92` `profile_user.followers.remove(request.user)`
- Self-follow is blocked by the `!=` guard (`:90`).
- Returns `partials/follow_button.html` on HTMX (`:99-107`) else redirects to `profile` (`:108`).

### Favorite / unfavorite — `apps/articles/views.py:197-208` `article_favorite_view`

# RealWorld E2E Test Selectors Contract

This document lists every CSS class, HTML attribute, text label, route, and
interface that the shared e2e tests depend on. Any RealWorld implementation
that wants to use these tests **must** provide all of the selectors below.

---

## Form Inputs (`name` attributes)

Inputs are located via the standard HTML `name` attribute.

| Selector                                     | Page                      |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `input[name="username"]`                     | Register, Settings        |
| `input[name="email"]`                        | Login, Register, Settings |
| `input[name="password"]`                     | Login, Register, Settings |
| `input[name="title"]`                        | Editor                    |
| `input[name="description"]`                  | Editor                    |
| `textarea[name="body"]`                      | Editor                    |
| `input[name="image"]`                        | Settings                  |
| `textarea[name="bio"]`                       | Settings                  |
| `input[placeholder="Enter tags"]`            | Editor                    |
| `textarea[placeholder="Write a comment..."]` | Article detail            |

---

## CSS Classes

### Layout & Navigation

| Class           | Element | Purpose               |
| --------------- | ------- | --------------------- |
| `.navbar`       | `nav`   | Main navigation bar   |
| `.navbar-brand` | `a`     | Logo / site name link |
| `.nav-link`     | `a`     | Navigation tab links  |
| `.banner`       | `div`   | Home page hero banner |
| `.container`    | `div`   | Page width container  |

### Feed & Articles

| Class                 | Element | Purpose                             |
| --------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `.feed-toggle`        | `div`   | Global Feed / Your Feed tab bar     |
| `.article-preview`    | `div`   | Article card in a feed list         |
| `.article-meta`       | `div`   | Author avatar + name + date         |
| `.article-content`    | `div`   | Rendered article body               |
| `.article-page`       | `div`   | Article detail page wrapper         |
| `.preview-link`       | `a`     | Clickable link wrapping the preview |
| `.author`             | `a`     | Author name in article meta         |
| `.empty-feed-message` | `div`   | "No articles here" placeholder      |

### Tags

| Class          | Element | Purpose                 |
| -------------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `.sidebar`     | `div`   | Home page sidebar       |
| `.tag-list`    | `div`   | Container for tag pills |
| `.tag-default` | `span`  | Base tag class          |
| `.tag-pill`    | `span`  | Pill-shaped tag         |

### Comments

Note there is a mix: `hx-select` on the profile page lets an HTMX link reuse the FULL-page view (no partial needed) by selecting a fragment client-side. For a notifications page, you can either follow the partial pattern or the `hx-select` pattern. ## 4. SELECTORS.md — `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-c-0/realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md` Full contents quoted (the file is the pinned e2e contract; breaking any selector fails the shared suite). Key sections relevant to a nav badge + notifications page: there is **no** existing notifications selector, so you are free to name new ones — but nav classes (`.navbar`, `.navbar-brand`, `.nav-link`), the `.container`, and the `Home` nav text are pinned and must not change. Form inputs (name attrs): `username`, `email`, `password`, `title`, `description`, `body`(textarea), `image`, `bio`(textarea), plus `input[placeholder="Enter tags"]` and `textarea[placeholder="Write a comment..."]`. Layout/Nav classes: `.navbar` (nav), `.navbar-brand` (a), `.nav-link` (a), `.banner` (div), `.container` (div). Feed/Articles: `.feed-toggle`, `.article-preview`, `.article-meta`, `.article-content`, `.article-page`, `.preview-link`, `.author`, `.empty-feed-message`. Tags: `.sidebar`, `.tag-list`, `.tag-default`, `.tag-pill`. Comments: `.card`, `.card-block`, `.comment-form`, `.comment-author-img`, `.mod-options`, `.ion-trash-a` (tests select posted comments with `.card:not(.comment-form) .card-block`). Profile: `.profile-page`, `.user-info`, `.user-img`, `.user-pic` (small navbar avatar). Pagination: `.pagination`, `.page-item` (active page has `active`). Buttons: `.btn-outline-primary` (favorite/not-yet), `.btn-primary` (unfavorite/already), `.btn-outline-danger` (logout/destructive). Errors: `.error-messages` (ul). Required text — Buttons: `Post Comment`, `Delete Article`, `Publish Article`, `Update Settings`, `Or click here to logout`, `Follow`/`Unfollow`, `Favorite`/`Unfavorite`, `Favorite Article`. Headings/Links: `Sign in`(h1), `Sign up`(h1), `Global Feed`(a.nav-link), `Your Feed`(a.nav-link), `Favorited`(a), `Edit Article`(a), `Edit Profile Settings`(a), `Home`(a.nav-link). Routes (pages): `/`, `/?feed=following`, `/?page=N`, `/tag/:tag`, `/tag/:tag?page=N`, `/login`, `/register`, `/editor`, `/editor/:slug`, `/settings`, `/profile/:username`, `/profile/:username/favorites`, `/article/:slug`. Templates use `{% load static %}` + `{% static 'css/styles.css' %}` etc. Static files present (only three): ``` static/css/styles.css static/images/conduit-logo.svg static/images/default-avatar.svg ``` `static/css/styles.css` is the RealWorld "conductor"/Conduit CSS. Icons come from ionicons 2.0.1 (CDN, `base.html:9`); the nav already uses `ion-compose`, `ion-gear-a`. A notification bell would conventionally be `ion-android-notifications` or similar from that set. Fonts are Google Fonts (Lora, Source Sans Pro). ### Implementation notes for the notifications feature - Add a new app or extend accounts; wire a `/notifications` route in one of the app `urls.py` files (all included at root via `config/urls.py:21-26`, no `/api` prefix). - Add the nav badge as a new `
  • ` inside the `{% if user.is_authenticated %}` block of `partials/header.html` (lines 9-25), following the active-link `request.resolver_match.url_name` pattern. - Expose the unread count either through `helpers/context_processors.py::conduit_context` (globally, so the nav renders it on every page) or via an HTMX-loaded badge partial. - Follow the "build context, then `is_htmx` at the bottom" view convention; create a full-page `templates/notifications/` template that `{% include %}`s a `templates/partials/` fragment returned on HTMX requests. - No `.badge` CSS exists — reuse `.counter` (`styles.css:1240`) or add a class; pick a new, non-pinned selector name since SELECTORS.md has no notifications entry. - `hx-headers` on `` already supplies CSRF for any `hx-post` mark-as-read actions.

# Notifications feature — spec/test discipline reference

This is an FFFlow **L3** project (`.ffflow/config.yaml`: `level: L3`, `stack: python`, `capture: github-issues`) with all four L3 features on: `property_based_testing`, `mutation_testing`, `rid_traceability`, `four_quality_gates`. Everything below is what a new "notifications" domain must match.

## 1. `docs/specs/` structure and Gherkin conventions

Layout (from `/home/claude/bench-ws/notifications-c-0/docs/specs/README.md:8-22`): one directory per bounded context, matching the Django apps + `helpers`. Acceptance specs live at the context root; domain/property specs under `<context>/domain/`. `*-properties.feature` files hold universal invariants tagged `@property-based`.

```
docs/specs/
  accounts/    authentication, profiles & following, user model
  articles/    feeds, authoring, article model, markdown
  comments/    commenting, comment model
  helpers/     pagination, integrity-error classification, htmx detection
  rid_map.<context>.yaml   (one per context, at specs root)
  README.md
```

**Conventions visible in the quoted `.feature` files above** (`docs/specs/comments/comments.feature`, `docs/specs/accounts/profiles-and-following.feature`, `docs/specs/comments/domain/comment.feature`, `docs/specs/articles/domain/article-properties.feature` — all quoted in full in my tool output):

- `Feature:` with a free-text `As a / I want / So that` narrative (comments.feature:1-6).
- Optional `Background:` block (profiles-and-following.feature:6-8).
- **`Rule:` blocks** group scenarios by business rule — every scenario lives under a `Rule:`. Example rules: "Adding a comment requires authentication", "A comment can only be deleted by its author or the article's author" (comments.feature:22, 68).
- **One `@RID-...` tag immediately above each `Scenario:`** — exactly one RID per scenario, on its own line (comments.feature:9, 16, 24…).
- **RID tag format** `@RID-{CONTEXT}-{NAME}-{NNN}` where CONTEXT is the uppercased first directory (`COMMENTS`, `ACCOUNTS`, `ARTICLES`, `HELPERS`); NAME is a sub-domain slug (`VIEW`, `AUTHZ`, `ADD`, `CONTENT`, `DELETE`, `SCOPING`, `INLINE`, `MODEL`, `ORDERING`, `CASCADE`, `PROFILE-VIEWER`, `FOLLOW-RESPONSE`…); NNN is a zero-padded 3-digit sequence within that NAME (comments.feature:9-148).
- Present-tense, domain-language `Given/When/Then/And` steps — no UI/implementation detail.
- **`# @unverified-intent:` comment** placed directly above the RID tag to pin currently-true-but-suspect behavior (comments.feature:50-51). README.md:62-67 explains: seven such scenarios exist project-wide; documented as contract, flagged for review, not silently fixed.
- **Property specs**: `*-properties.feature` files use `Scenario Outline` + `Examples:` and carry **two tags** `@property-based @RID-...` on one line (pagination-properties.feature:11, 28, 45; article-properties.feature:11, 26, 42, 49). These are DB-free universal invariants bound to Hypothesis.

## 2. The RID system

`docs/specs/README.md:24-49` is the authority. RIDs are the traceability anchor: **spec → test → code**. Project total: **131 scenarios, 131 RIDs** (README.md:30).

**Format** (README.md:26-28): `@RID-{CONTEXT}-{NAME}-{NNN}`. The CONTEXT segment **must** match the first directory under `docs/specs/`. This match is enforced by `specdrive audit`.

**Where the spec↔test mapping lives**: the Django test runner cannot emit per-test JUnit properties, so the mapping is externalized in `docs/specs/rid_map.<context>.yaml` files, keyed `"<classname>::<test_method>": [RID-...]` (README.md:42-49). `scripts/inject_rids.py` writes these into the JUnit report as `<property name="rid" value="RID-...">` elements (inject_rids.py:31-54).

**rid_map format** (quoted fully above — `docs/specs/rid_map.comments.yaml:1-29`): a YAML header comment naming the tests file and spec files, then one entry per test method. Key = dotted classname `comments.tests.CommentCreateViewTest::test_create_comment`, value = a **list** of RIDs. Notable properties observed across all maps:

- **One test can cover multiple RIDs** — `test_create_comment: [RID-COMMENTS-ADD-001, RID-COMMENTS-INLINE-003]` (rid_map.comments.yaml:7).
- **The same RID can appear on multiple tests** — `RID-COMMENTS-CONTENT-001/002` both come from `test_empty_body_is_noop`; `RID-ACCOUNTS-LOGIN`… etc. `rid_map.helpers.yaml` shows `RID-HELPERS-PAGINATE-PROP-*` reused across several `PaginateTest` methods (rid_map.helpers.yaml:31-57).
- **`@NOSPEC`** marks deliberately-unmapped tests — seed/CLI management commands and bare GET-render smoke tests (README.md:47-49; rid_map.articles.yaml:35-37, 70-77; rid_map.accounts.yaml:23,31,53-54; rid_map.helpers.yaml `@NOSPEC` entries). Written either `["@NOSPEC"]` or `- '@NOSPEC'`. 15 tests are unmapped project-wide.
- **Property-suite RIDs** live in a separate `docs/specs/rid_map.property.yaml` keyed by pytest nodeid `specs.property.test_pagination_properties::test_pagination_003` (rid_map.property.yaml:1-8). The `[param]` suffix of parametrized cases is stripped at injection (inject_rids.py:37-39).

**How uniqueness / correctness is kept**: `just spec-audit` → `npx specdrive audit` checks every RID is well-formed, unique, and CONTEXT-matches its directory (README.md:33-35). `just spec-verify` → `npx specdrive verify` with `strictTraceability: true` (specdrive.yaml:16) checks full spec→test coverage: **131/131 covered, 0 uncovered, and no untraced test** (README.md:36-39).

**Allocating RIDs for a new "notifications" domain** — to match the discipline exactly:

1. Create `docs/specs/notifications/` with acceptance `.feature` files at the root and any `notifications/domain/*.feature` for model/property specs.
2. Every scenario gets exactly one `@RID-NOTIFICATIONS-{NAME}-{NNN}` tag. CONTEXT **must** be `NOTIFICATIONS` (uppercased dir name) or `specdrive audit` fails. Pick NAME sub-slugs by rule (e.g. `NOTIFICATIONS-VIEW-001`, `NOTIFICATIONS-MARK-READ-001`, `NOTIFICATIONS-AUTHZ-001`, `NOTIFICATIONS-MODEL-001`, `NOTIFICATIONS-CASCADE-001`), numbering from `001` within each NAME.
3. Create `docs/specs/rid_map.notifications.yaml` with the header-comment convention, mapping `notifications.tests.<Class>::<method>` → RID lists. Mark seed/CLI/smoke tests `@NOSPEC`.
4. **Critical wiring step — update the `justfile` `spec-verify` recipe**: `merge_rid_maps.py` is invoked with an **explicit hardcoded list** of the four current maps (justfile, `spec-verify` recipe: `docs/specs/rid_map.accounts.yaml docs/specs/rid_map.articles.yaml docs/specs/rid_map.comments.yaml docs/specs/rid_map.helpers.yaml`). You must add `docs/specs/rid_map.notifications.yaml` to that command or the new RIDs won't be injected and `specdrive verify` will report them uncovered. (The `rid_map.property.yaml` is injected separately in step 2 of that recipe.)
5. Any `@property-based` scenarios also need binding in `specs/property/` and an entry in `rid_map.property.yaml`.

## 3. Unit test structure

`apps/comments/tests.py` is quoted in full above (168 lines). Conventions to mirror:

- Module docstring `"""Unit tests for comments app — views."""` (tests.py:1).
- `User = get_user_model()` and a module-level `make_user(...)` factory helper (tests.py:13-17).
- One `TestCase` subclass **per view/behavior cluster**: `CommentCreateViewTest`, `ArticleCommentListViewTest`, `CommentContentTrimTest`, `CommentModelTest`, `CommentDeleteViewTest`. Class names map 1:1 to rid_map keys.
- `setUp` builds fixtures via ORM (`Article.objects.create(...)`, `make_user(...)`).
- Views tested through **`self.client`** (`django.test.Client`): `self.client.post(reverse("comment_create", args=[...]), {...})`, `self.client.force_login(user)`, `self.client.get(...)`.
- HTMX branch tested by passing `HTTP_HX_REQUEST="true"` and asserting `status_code == 200` + `assertContains` (tests.py:46-54, 170-176).
- Assertions: `assertRedirects`, `assertEqual`, `assertContains`, `resp.context[...]`, `Comment.objects.count()`, `.exists()`, 403/404 status checks.
- Model tests exercise attribution, timestamps, ordering, and FK cascade delete (tests.py:95-126).
- **RIDs are NOT referenced in the test file at all** — no docstrings, no comments. The test method name is the sole join key; the RID linkage lives **entirely** in `docs/specs/rid_map.<context>.yaml`. So test method names must be stable and descriptive.
- **Property tests inside the Django suite**: `hypothesis.extra.django` classes (e.g. `SlugStabilityPropertyTest`, `UserIdentityPropertyTest`, `FollowGraphSelfPropertyTest`) live in the same `apps/*/tests.py` for DB-backed invariants and are mapped in the normal rid_map (rid_map.articles.yaml:11-12, rid_map.accounts.yaml:18-20). README.md:52-59 splits the two suites.

## 4. E2E Playwright tests

`playwright/CLAUDE.md` (quoted in full above) is the authority. Key facts:

- **Test files are vendored upstream** at `realworld/specs/e2e/*.spec.ts` — the shared RealWorld spec, shared across all implementations including API ones. **Never edit the vendored copy** (playwright/CLAUDE.md:32-34). These are NOT RID-annotated and are separate from the FFFlow spec/RID system.
- Files: `articles`, `auth`, `comments`, `settings`, `social`, `navigation`, `url-navigation`, `error-handling`, `health`, `null-fields`, `user-fetch-errors`, `xss-security` `.spec.ts`, plus `helpers/*.ts` (auth, articles, comments, profile, api, config, setup, debug) and `playwright.base.ts`, `SELECTORS.md`.
- **Harness** (`playwright/playwright.config.ts`, quoted in full above): `testDir: '../realworld/specs/e2e'`, `fullyParallel: false`, `workers: 1`, chromium only. The `webServer` block auto-starts Django via `uv run python -c "... migrate; seed_data; runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 --noreload"` with `DEBUG=True`, in-memory SQLite `file:memdb1?mode=memory&cache=shared`, `USE_FAST_HASHER=True`. Torn down on exit.
- **API_MODE**: ~65 tests are API-only and self-skip via `test.skip(!API_MODE, ...)` (see health.spec.ts:16, comments.spec.ts). Default here is `API_MODE=false`.
- **Baseline**: **74 passed, 65 skipped, 0 failed** (playwright/CLAUDE.md:20; echoed in root CLAUDE.md). Deviation is the signal.
- Run via `just integration-test` → `cd playwright && npx playwright test` (npx not bun, per playwright/CLAUDE.md:22-24).
- Tests drive the browser through the register/login flow (e.g. comments.spec.ts:10-17 registers a fresh user + creates an article in `beforeEach`), locating elements by the **`SELECTORS.md` contract** (CSS classes, `name` attributes, text labels). Root CLAUDE.md warns: never rename form field names or visible labels without checking `realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md` — the e2e suite pins them.
- **For a notifications feature**: since e2e files are vendored upstream and not RID-mapped, a notifications UI must simply keep the baseline green (and add any new selectors to the contract upstream if needed). E2e is not part of the RID traceability count.

## 5. `specdrive.yaml` and audit/verify

`specdrive.yaml` (quoted in full above): `localSpecs: [docs/specs]`, `strictTraceability: true`. Docs at github.com/bryonjacob/specdrive.

- **`just spec-audit`** → `npx specdrive audit`: validates RID format, uniqueness, and CONTEXT-vs-directory match. Blocking. Also reported by `just spec-status`.
- **`just spec-verify`** (justfile, full recipe visible in my first tool output): the full traceability pipeline —
  1. `scripts/merge_rid_maps.py` merges the four per-context maps into `test-reports/rid_map.django.yaml`.
  2. Runs the Django suite (`manage.py test apps helpers`) with `TEST_OUTPUT_DIR=test-reports` → `junit.xml`, then `inject_rids.py` stamps RIDs in.
  3. Runs the pytest property suite (`pytest specs/property/`) → `property.xml`, injects `rid_map.property.yaml`.
  4. `merge_junit.py` combines both → `merged.xml`.
  5. `npx specdrive verify test-reports/merged.xml` enforces `strictTraceability` (every RID covered, every test traced or `@NOSPEC`).
- `just check-all` runs `format lint typecheck coverage spec-audit spec-verify` (justfile). Both spec gates are blocking and part of `check-all`.

## 6. Coverage + property + mutation

- **Coverage**: root CLAUDE.md — "100% actual, 96% floor". `just coverage` runs `coverage run -m manage test apps helpers` then `coverage report --fail-under=96` and an HTML report (justfile `coverage` recipe). `.coveragerc` (quoted above): `source = apps,helpers,config`; omits migrations, `asgi.py`, `wsgi.py`, `manage.py`; `exclude_lines` cover `pragma: no cover`, `TYPE_CHECKING`, `raise NotImplementedError`, env-specific `SystemExit`/`USE_FAST_HASHER` branches, and the `except ImportError` psycopg2 fallback. A notifications app must land at 100% actual and stay ≥96%.
- **Property-based testing** (Hypothesis): two mechanisms. (a) In-Django `hypothesis.extra.django` `TestCase` property classes for DB-backed invariants (slug stability, email-identity, self-follow), mapped in the normal rid_maps. (b) The dedicated **property suite** `specs/property/` under pytest + `pytest-bdd` + `pytest-bdd-property`, which binds `@property-based` Gherkin `Scenario Outline`s **directly to the feature file** and generates 100+ inputs per scenario. `specs/property/test_pagination_properties.py` (quoted in full above) shows the pattern: `@scenario(_FEATURE, "<exact scenario name>")` stubs, `register_strategy(...)` for the `<placeholder>` nouns, and `@property_when` / `@property_then` step regexes. pyproject.toml:96-103 scopes pytest to `specs/property/` so it never double-collects the Django suite. A notifications invariant would get a `*-properties.feature`, a `@property-based @RID-NOTIFICATIONS-...-PROP-NNN` tag, a binding module in `specs/property/`, and a `rid_map.property.yaml` entry.
- **Mutation testing**: declared as an L3 feature flag (`.ffflow/config.yaml:18 mutation_testing: true`; `.ffflow/CLAUDE.md:10`) and named in the audit state (`.ffflow/audit.yaml`). **However, there is no mutation tool wired into the repo** — grep across `justfile`, `Makefile`, `pyproject.toml`, and `.github/workflows/` finds no `mutmut`/`cosmic-ray`/`mutation` invocation or dependency. The only references are the two FFFlow config mentions. So mutation testing is a declared L3 aspiration/gate enforced through the FFFlow workflow (the `fff:quality-gates` / `fff:total-specification` skills), not an automated recipe you inherit. For notifications, expect it to be driven by the FFFlow audit/quality-gate skills rather than a `just` target — verify with the maintainer whether a runner is expected before adding one (and note the CLAUDE.md rule against introducing new tooling/timeouts unasked).

## Key gotchas for the notifications app (from module CLAUDE.md files)

- **App layering is one-way** (`apps/CLAUDE.md`): `accounts → articles`, `comments → articles`; `articles` is the center and imports nothing from the others. Decide notifications' place in this DAG; the architecture auditor checks import direction (`.ffflow/audit.yaml` architecture block, 0 violations).
- **`apps/` is on `sys.path`** (`config/settings.py`) — imports are `from articles.models import Article`, **not** `from apps.articles...`. This is load-bearing for tests, URLs, and the app registry.
- **Never use Django reverse-FK `_set` accessors** (e.g. `article.comment_set`) — `django-types` doesn't type them and `ty` warns; use `Model.objects.filter(...)` (`apps/comments/CLAUDE.md`).
- Views should be **HTMX-aware** via `helpers.htmx.is_htmx`: return a `partials/*.html` fragment on HTMX requests, redirect on plain posts (comments pattern, tested with `HTTP_HX_REQUEST="true"`).
- Root CLAUDE.md hard rules: **never** raise timeouts, **never** use `# type: ignore`, **never** rename pinned form fields/labels without checking `SELECTORS.md`.

**Files to create/modify for notifications**, to match the pattern exactly:
- `docs/specs/notifications/*.feature` (+ `domain/*.feature`), RID-tagged.
- `docs/specs/rid_map.notifications.yaml`.
- `apps/notifications/tests.py` (+ `models.py`, `views.py`, `urls.py`, `CLAUDE.md`, migrations).
- **Edit `justfile` `spec-verify`** to add the new rid_map to the `merge_rid_maps.py` argument list.
- Update `docs/specs/README.md` scenario/RID counts and the layout list.
- Optionally `specs/property/` bindings + `rid_map.property.yaml` for any invariants.
